messages:
anika: Heads-up — we should settle who owns 'eviction' semantics across Hosted / Dedicated / Private. We've got inconsistencies during canaries and tenant cache invalidation.
kevin: Do you mean eviction as in runtime KV cache eviction, or control-plane policy-driven evict (like rollout-driven flush)?
maria: Both. Private can't assume control-plane reachability, so semantics need to be portable and observable.
tom: Quick take: split responsibilities. Runtime provides primitive ops + events. Control plane provides intent/policy and a best-effort orchestrator.
anika: Sketch of the minimal runtime-facing contract I had in mind:
```
interface HostAdapter {
  Evict(namespace string, keyPrefix string) -> EvictResult
  GetCacheInfo(namespace string) -> CacheMetrics
  SubscribeEvictEvents(callbackUri string) -> SubscriptionId
  QueryCapabilities() -> ["evict", "prefetch", "namespace-level-flush"]
}
```
kevin: Nice. We should also standardize error codes so callers (console, control plane) can react deterministically. e.g., `RT_EVICT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` -> 501, `RT_EVICT_CONFLICT` -> 409, `RT_EVICT_TEMP_FAIL` -> 503.
maria: Telemetry note: every eviction event should include `host.mode` (hosted|dedicated|private), `evict.trigger` (controlplane|api|healthcheck|manual), and a hashed `tenant_id`. No PII.
tom: Edgecase: Dedicated with shared GPU pools — eviction must be tenant-scoped but there are cross-tenant eviction side effects when memory pressure is global. We need an explicit contract for "best-effort" vs "guaranteed" evictions in that scenario.
anika: Agreed. Also need UI/ops surfaces: a console action to force-evict per-tenant + audit entry, and a runbook step for Private (since support can't call control plane).
runtime-bot: deploy: runtime-v3.4.1 — added optional `Evict(namespace,keyPrefix)` hook (flag `--enable-evict-hook`).
kevin: Ops / runbook implications: add a CLI for oncall: `redwoodctl runtime evict --tenant T --ns cache --prefix p` and a metric `evict.attempts` with `evict.outcome`. I'll take error-code mapping and deprecation plan for legacy endpoints.
maria: I'll update runbooks and console action flows (including audit and confirmation modal).
tom: I'll prototype the HostAdapter shim + capability probe and a fallback where Private nodes expose a sidecar HTTP endpoint when control-plane is offline.
anika: Decision items (assigns): [1] Define HostAdapter contract + capability matrix (Tom). [2] Error-code mapping + deprecate old eviction API (Kevin). [3] Runbooks + console UI + telemetry tags (Maria). [4] RFC PR with examples + acceptance tests (Anika).
kevin: Timeline?
anika: RFC PR by EOW (Fri). Tom prototype for Dedicated by next sprint. Maria runbook changes staged next week. Kevin will draft deprecation notes.
maria: :thumbsup: I'll also add a short evaluation test that simulates control-plane loss to validate Private behaviour.
ops-summon-bot: Reminder: oncall rotation updated — Kevin is primary for the next 2 weeks.
anika: Thanks — I'll open the RFC PR now and link the prototype issue in the thread.
runtime-bot: link: https://git.redwood/example/rfcs/eviction-contracts (draft)
kevin: Thanks everyone. We'll iterate fast; if anyone sees any compatibility concerns add them to the PR.
